Highlander was one of those films that came at the perfect time and captured imaginations. The original film spawned several sequels, a handful of television shows, and a novelization. However, a reboot never happened, even though Summit Entertainment announced in 2008 that it was remaking the original movie.

Now, however, the long wait is almost over. Starring Henry Cavill as Connor MacLeod, Amazon MGM's upcoming movie promises everything fans loved about the original, plus serious John Wick energy, as first-look footage for the Highlander reboot revealed at CinemaCon 2026. Since principal photography only began in early 2026, though, it will still be quite a while before the film arrives.

In the meantime, Highlander fans can tide themselves over with other excellent television shows with similar vibes to the original movie, exploring narrative elements like time travel and immortality that made the film such a cult favorite. The protagonist in the show is Duncan MacLeod, an Immortal who has lived for 400 years, but took himself out of the Game by hiding from other Immortals.

Duncan MacLeod's Immortal journey primarily examines his relationships, whether they be with other Immortals or mortals. Throughout the series, he loves and loses people several times, fights numerous others like himself, and learns about the Watchers, a secret society that records the history of the Immortals. Overall, the series shares many themes with the films, but it also reveals more backstory about Duncan and the Immortals in general. While it isn't the same as the Highlander film, Highlander: The Series is the closest someone can get to it while waiting to see Connor MacLeod on the big screen once again.

Forever Knight featured Nick Knight, a vampire who was also a detective and was eager to shed his immortality and become human once again. Honestly, in some ways, this show is a bit of a rip-off of Highlander, not only because it features an immortal who wants to become human, but also because the vampires on this show had a warning sense about each other, just as the Immortals do. The show also contains many flashbacks to the main character's previous lifetimes.

However similar the two were, this show stood on its own as a fun urban fantasy show, which followed Nick's struggle to protect innocent people to make up for the sins of his past lives as a killer, while also trying to keep the secrets of the vampire world away from any humans in his life. Unfortunately, Forever Knight's series finale was hated by fans, sparking quite a bit of controversy.
